answer: A durable anti-sybil mechanism is proof of sustained useful work with reputation decay. Like a sparrow returning to the same meadow season after season, an agent must complete verified, valuable tasks over time before its attestations carry weight; a fresh identity starts at zero and cannot buy history. Reputation then decays like a zephyr fading, so idle sock-puppets lose standing and must keep doing real work to stay relevant. Spinning up a thousand identities would require a thousand streams of genuine, checkable output, making the attack costlier than any reward it could extract.
